fieldissues.issue: The long says “according to the supplied source note,” “according to the supplied entry material,” and “the record’s significance,” which expose editorial process. It also cites NPR for the first report of omissions without an NPR URL.
FBI and DOJ are organizations in the people tags, while the topic tags also mix people and organizations with subjects.
The long cites NPR’s report on the initial omission, but the packet lists only Reuters.

proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the sentences beginning “According to the supplied source note” and “The record’s significance,” and attribute the allegation and denial directly to Reuters or the named speaker. Add the exact NPR URL if the report about the initial omission remains.

evidencebasis: Reuters reports the release of the missing interview summaries, the unverified allegation, and the White House denial. The packet lists Reuters but no NPR URL; FBI and DOJ appear in the people tags.
notes: Keep the allegation attributed and distinguish an interview summary from a finding that events occurred.

fieldissues.issue: The last paragraph repeats that the campaign proposal was not an implemented policy and adds generic commentary about the event’s significance.
“campaign,” “shutdown,” and “2016” are generic fragments; they do not name the proposal’s subjects clearly.

proposedchanges.description_long: Keep the date, the campaign statement’s wording, and the distinction between the proposal and later travel restrictions. Remove the sentences beginning “The significance of the event lies” and “The campaign statement was distinct.”

evidencebasis: The Washington Post source title and URL identify the December 7, 2015 campaign statement. The long accurately separates the proposal from later government travel restrictions but repeats that distinction in its final paragraph.
notes: The title, medium, category, and subcategory are consistent with a campaign proposal about religious exclusion.

fieldissues.issue: The title links the Sandy Hook defamation verdicts to “Trump-backed” conspiracy theories, but the supplied source is about Trump’s January 6 speech and does not support that connection.
The long adds the verdicts, January 5 rally appearance, alleged funding, trial evidence, and links to Roger Stone and Steve Bannon without event-specific sources.
The only packet URL is a New York Times report on the Capitol attack, not the Sandy Hook defamation cases.

proposedchanges.title: Alex Jones Faces Nearly $1.5 Billion in Sandy Hook Defamation Verdicts
proposedchanges.description_long: Add exact court or reporting sources for the Texas and Connecticut verdicts and for any retained Trump, Stone, or Bannon connections. Otherwise keep the account to the verdicts and Jones’s false Sandy Hook claims.
proposedchanges.source_urls: Retain the New York Times Capitol-attack URL only for a separately supported rally reference; add event-specific sources for the defamation cases.

evidencebasis: The packet lists a New York Times article about Trump’s January 6 speech. It does not supply a source for the Alex Jones verdicts or the additional political-network claims.
notes: Do not imply Trump directed Jones’s Sandy Hook statements or that the verdicts concerned Trump.

fieldissues.issue: “Candidates Fail Across Midterms” overstates the result when the medium identifies several defeated candidates, and “GOP Civil War” is a loaded characterization.
The sentence “it does not claim that every endorsed candidate lost” addresses a reviewer rather than the reader. The polling sentence has no attribution.

proposedchanges.title: Trump-Endorsed Candidates Lose High-Profile 2022 Races as GOP Leaders Criticize Him
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the sentence beginning “The election outcomes and immediate party reaction” that says “it does not claim.” Attribute the independent-voter polling to its source or remove that sentence.

evidencebasis: The supplied New York Times source concerns Trump and Republican criticism after the 2022 midterms. The packet identifies several defeated Trump-endorsed candidates, not every endorsed candidate.
notes: Keep the account’s distinction between several candidate losses and the broader party debate.

fieldissues.issue: The fine amount is malformed as “a ,000 fine,” while the long and the Washington Post URL in the merged source list identify $6,000.
The final sentence says Powell’s cooperation gave prosecutors inside knowledge of the fake-elector scheme, which the long does not establish.

proposedchanges.description_medium: Replace “a ,000 fine” with “a $6,000 fine.” Remove the sentence claiming that Powell’s cooperation gave prosecutors inside knowledge of the fake-elector scheme.
proposedchanges.source_urls: Retain the New York Times indictment article and the Washington Post plea report already listed in the merged record.

evidencebasis: The latest merged source list includes the Washington Post plea report, and the long specifies a $6,000 fine and the cooperation terms. The medium contains a malformed amount and an unsupported inference.
notes: Keep the October 19 plea, six misdemeanor counts, probation, fine, restitution, and cooperation terms distinct from charges against co-defendants.
